title: Internal quartic ZAFF fit, protected asymptotics and spurious-minimum regularization
summary: Zero-close the internal bonded field, fit native ZAFF forms, preserve its fourth-order jet during asymptotic completion and minima regularization, and only then transform to normal modes.
gates: Missing internal cubic/quartic derivatives are zero by an explicit initial model closure, not new measured zeros
No independent four-distinct internal quartic parameters
Internal derivative inputs and complete baseline jets are bound to the exact parent and primitive gauge
Fit the internal bonded quartic using ZAFF native functions before any final normal-mode transformation
External conditions may constrain only angular boundaries or dihedral periodicity; no joint nonlocal E/G/H calibration
Every completion and regularization term has an algebraically vanishing reference jet through fourth order
Regularize candidate spurious minima only after a field-only search with explicit physical basins, domain, starts and strength policy
Failed searches, boundary hits and residual saddles never pass the minima gate
Normal transformation retains induced four-distinct entries and geometric chain-rule terms
Frozen nonbonded field remains separate and unchanged
No electronic points are acquired and no QM keywords are introduced
Numerical execution requires the explicitly declared remote host and 128 GiB
coordinate_policy: Frozen internal primitive gauge; missing entries closed before fitting; completed field transformed afterwards. Bonded modal output is labelled separately from frozen nonbonded.
backend_policy: Resident native field only. Finite multistart minima checks do not prove global absence of all other basins.
